text:
anjali: FYI customer acme-inc escalated — large p99 spike after runtime v4.12 canary rolled out to eu-west-1 at ~03:40 UTC. They say p95 also moved up ~40ms and p99 doubled. Posting logs they captured. Escalating to runtime.

mike: ack. do we have the canary rollout id? link to rollout dashboard?

anjali: deploy-bot shows: canary roll id 2026-03-15-0312-v4.12. Here's the CDN/latency dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/canary/2026-03-15-0312 . customer request samples attached in thread.

sara: quick question — is this only eu-west-1? any signs in us-east or ap-south canaries?

raj: I see a small delta in us-east instances too but not as severe. eu-west p99 jumped from 160ms -> ~380ms at 03:47 UTC. Can confirm metric spike aligned with canary window.

deploy-bot: canary rollout 2026-03-15-0312: 30% traffic -> 100% canary group A (eu-west-1). No auto-rollback triggered.

mike: any known change in kernel selector or batching defaults in this patch? v4.12 release notes mention "kv-cache eviction fix" and "kernel selector heuristics tweak".

sara: that kernel selector tweak could route to a different matmul kernel for short sequences — might increase tail latency if it triggers a slower fallback on some GPUs.

anjali: customer payloads are short prompts (avg 52 tokens). they also show intermittent TLS handshake spikes but main correlator is token generation latency.

raj: let's bisect config: try forcing kernel selector to previous heuristic on a canary instance and measure. Also try disabling the kv-cache eviction change — that might cause extra cache misses and increase early token latencies.

ops-jen: I can spin a private canary in eu-west-1 with v4.12 but kernel-selector=legacy and kv-cache=true/false toggles. Which order?

mike: order: 1) kernel-selector=legacy; 2) kv-cache=old; 3) revert quantization profile (if any). Keep dataset short requests.

sara: also add a small synthetic workload that mimics acme-inc headers and concurrency to reproduce.

anjali: customer provided request-id 6b9f2a2f and sample payload. putting them in test harness now.

support-bot: running quick smoke on prod-staging -> baseline p95 120ms, p99 180ms. Will run with kernel-selector=legacy.

(5m later)

support-bot: Result: kernel-selector=legacy on a canary instance reduced p99 from 380ms -> 170ms for the sampled workloads. p95 also back near baseline.

raj: ok that's a strong signal. The kernel selector tweak is likely culprit. What changed exactly in heuristics? Anyone on the kernel PR?

mike: PR #3412 changed cost threshold when selecting matmul path for seq_len < 64. It favored a cached-tensor path that on certain Ampere cards has higher worst-case latency under our contending batch patterns.

sara: that matches: acme's traffic pattern has lots of small concurrent requests, so contention + the new kernel's scheduling causes tail amplification.

anjali: mitigation options: 1) emergency rollback of kernel selector heuristic (quick) 2) patch to add per-device override to continue using legacy path for affected GPU types 3) targeted rollout freeze to prevent v4.12 out of eu-west-1

mike: rollout freeze + per-device override seems safest short-term. But if we can flip kernel-selector back remotely, do that now to stop customer impact.

ops-jen: I can patch config flag and push delta to control plane. command I will run:

```
kubectl patch configmap/runtime-flags -n infra --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/kernel_selector","value":"legacy"}]'
```

raj: before doing that, confirm no other customers depend on the heuristic for perf improvements. Could degrade throughput elsewhere.

sara: quick runbook: revert in canary first (we already have signal). If no regressions in 10m, push to remaining regions. Notify support to temp-upper-limit rollout.

anjali: @support-bot please notify acme-inc we're investigating and ask for additional sample request-ids and whether they see the spike for embeddings too (they only reported generation so far).

support-bot: Message sent to customer at 03:58 UTC. Asked for request-ids and a cURL example. :eyes:

(6m later)

ops-jen: patched configmap -> kernel_selector=legacy on eu-west canaries. Monitoring...

deploy-bot: configmap update observed by 4 of 4 runtime pods in eu-west-1 at 04:06 UTC. Rolling apply complete.

support-bot: preliminary: p99 dropped back to ~170ms within 2 minutes of flag flip. acme confirms latency normalized for a 10-min window. They still saw a couple of spikes but tolerable.

mike: good. Root cause triage: kernel selector heuristic + Ampere scheduling interaction + high small-request concurrency = tail latency regression. We should revert the PR or gate it behind per-device profiling.

raj: I'll open a rollback PR that restores previous default and adds a device-based opt-in. Also add perf test to CI that runs small-request concurrency on Ampere to catch this.

sara: add an automated canary metric check for p95/p99 deltas vs baseline > 20% that blocks rollout. It exists but thresholds were too loose. Lowering to 15% for tail metrics.

anjali: action items:
- ops-jen: keep kernel_selector=legacy until PR #3412 is updated (done) (owner: ops-jen)
- raj: rollback PR + device opt-in + perf CI test (owner: raj)
- mike: update release notes and patch notes re: heuristics and add KB article (owner: mike)
- support-bot: follow up with customer and mark support ticket high priority (owner: support-bot)
- sara: tighten canary p95/p99 thresholds and add region-based alerts (owner: sara)

ops-jen: copying the quick commands I used:
```
# check current flag
kubectl get configmap runtime-flags -n infra -o yaml

# patch to legacy
kubectl patch configmap/runtime-flags -n infra --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/kernel_selector","value":"legacy"}]'

# verify pods reloaded
kubectl rollout status deployment/runtime-node -n infra
```

support-bot: ticket updated. customer provided extra request-ids; support will share once we run them through log correlator.

anjali: thanks all. keep this thread updated with rollback PR link and perf test results. Reopen if anything reoccurs. :thumbsup:
